newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- US T-bond futures seen toppish near-term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- US T-bond futures seen toppish near-term.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures may be putting in a short-term top after several tentative-looking pushes to four-month highs this week, although the underlying trend remains bullish, technical analysts said.
David Lundgren, a senior technical analyst at Technical Data, said the market looked vulnerable to a corrective downturn, citing a number of bearish patterns on the daily candlestick chart this week.
"It's really just that the candlestick picture is very clouded," he said. "It shows a lot of uncertainty."
He pointed out, however, that momentum indicators like the ADX trend-strength reading and the moving average convergence/divergence (MACD) for longer periods were maintaining a bullish bias.

"All that stuff, especially in the longer timeframe like the weekly and the monthly, are starting to turn really positive," he said. "That being the case, any weakness that you have in the day timeframe is something you'd want to buy."
David Lockwood, senior interest-rate analyst at Elliott Wave International, agreed that the longer-term uptrend was probably intact.
"The main point is that it's still in the rally from the April low and it's going to be for quite a while," he said.
He predicted that the latest up move from the May 27 low would likely top out in the 112-11/32 to 112-20/32 area to be followed by a pullback, perhaps toward 110-23/32.
"I think we'll see a top today," he said.
But he noted that Elliott Wave patterns since April have been hard to identify, making projections difficult.
"Part of the rally up from the April low has been five-waves...but it's hard to count exactly where those five-waves are in there," he said.
Lundgren said 112-15/32 was a major resistance for September T-bonds, and a failure to close above that level could set the stage for consolidative trading next week.
The contract briefly rose to a fresh high at 112-18/32 in mid-morning trade but has since pulled back somewhat.
Lundgren said a failure to maintain gains would probably result in another bearish daily candlestick -- after several already marked this week -- plus a bearish weekly candlestick.

The market's latest development had begun with an "advance block" and a "dark cloud cover", both bearish signals, he said. They were temporary offset by a "bullish engulfing" on Wednesday, but reinforced by Thursday's "long-legged doji".

"If the bond pulls back into the area where it opened, you'll end up with a long-legged doji on the weekly chart," he added. A long-legged doji occurs when the open and the close are roughly the same, with long shadows on either side.
